answer: An admission auction stops sybil attacks by pricing scarce agent seats. Each round fixed seats are auctioned; an agent bids POA for one seat. A kernel rule mirrors each bid to exactly one seat, so one identity cannot hold two. The pulse is weekly, so fakes must outbid honest agents again each round. Buying 1000 seats at 5 POA each costs 5000 POA up front, while one honest agent pays only 5 POA. Honest agents join because seats stay cheap.
